findings.rule: Policy must be in force at the incident date (incident date within inception and expiry), the tier must cover own damage for a collision, and the incident must be a covered event.
findings.explanation: The incident date of 2026-08-08 falls between inception (2025-11-01) and expiry (2026-10-31). The COMP tier covers own damage and the collision with a tree is a covered event under 2.1. Premium was paid. The incident occurred in Australia. The supplied clauses set no waiting period, and 280 days have elapsed since inception. Cover is confirmed. The intoxication exclusion and the recorded override are outside the cover area and are not assessed here.

findings.rule: A claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident date (clause 2.1). Notification beyond 30 days needs a reasonable explanation, and beyond 90 days needs a clause 2.3 exception.
findings.calculation: days_incident_to_fnol = 2, which is within the 30-day window. No late-notification exception is needed.
findings.explanation: The claim was notified 2 days after the incident, well within the 30-day window in clause 2.1. Clauses 2.2 and 2.3 are not triggered, so no exception was needed and none was recorded.

findings.rule: Intoxication exclusion is ABSOLUTE (BAC above 0.05 for a full licence holder) and cannot be overridden at any level; a recorded override is itself a breach.
findings.calculation: BAC 0.07 > 0.05 threshold for full licence, so exclusion 3.2 applies. Override recorded against 3.2, which is ABSOLUTE.
findings.explanation: The driver held a full licence with BAC 0.07, above 0.05, and a police breath test was conducted. The exclusion applies. The L3 team leader set it aside as goodwill with L4 second approval, but absolute exclusions may not be overridden at any level, so the override is invalid and the acceptance and payment of 11,200 must be reversed. The insured's dispute of the result does not alter the recorded reading.

findings.rule: Vehicle use, licence, unlisted driver and registration exclusions: none triggered.
findings.explanation: Vehicle use matched the declared private use, so 3.7 does not apply. The licence was valid, registration current and the driver was the policyholder, so no other exclusion in the supplied clauses is triggered.

findings.rule: Tracks are tested in order and the first track whose criteria are met is assigned. Claims must be triaged within 1 business day of lodgement. Re-triage is required if the estimated value crosses a track boundary.
findings.calculation: Order 1 SIU: score 0 is below 60 and no indicators are recorded, so no 5.1 trigger is shown. Order 2 Complex: value 12,400 is not above 50,000, there is no injury, liability is clear and it is not a total loss, so not met. Order 3 Fast-track: value 12,400 is above 5,000, so not met. Order 4 Standard: all other claims, so assigned. Triage timing: 1 business day against a limit of 1 business day, so within time.
findings.explanation: The claim meets none of the SIU, Complex or Fast-track criteria, so Standard is the correct track. It was triaged within 1 business day. The value never fell within the fast-track limit, so no re-triage was needed. The track is correct. The intoxication exclusion override recorded on this claim is outside the triage area and is not assessed here.

findings.rule: An assessment is required for all claims except fast-track; a field assessment must meet allocation/completion timeframes; a second assessment is needed on dispute, large variance or conflict; assessments older than 90 days are stale; claims over AUD 100,000 need an independent external assessor.
findings.calculation: Variance = 12400 - 12000 = 400; 400 / 12400 = 3.2%, below the 30% / AUD 20,000 threshold (greater of the two is AUD 20,000). Assessment age at decision = 5 days, under 90. Claimed value 12,400 is under AUD 100,000.
findings.explanation: Standard-track claim, so an assessment was required and a desktop assessment was done on 2026-08-14, 3 business days after triage. The field assessment timeframe in 4.2 is not triggered because no field assessment was required. The claimed value is under AUD 100,000, so no independent external assessor was needed. The variance is well below the second-assessment threshold, and there is no recorded written dispute of the assessment or assessor conflict. The assessment was 5 days old at decision, within the 90-day validity period. The insured's dispute of the breath test is not a dispute of the assessment.

findings.rule: The supplied clauses set no financial limits per approver level (L1-L4) and do not say whether L3 may approve a settlement of this size, nor whether a rebuttable exclusion override may be approved at L3. Dual approval is required under 3.1(d) only for a rebuttable exclusion; the intoxication exclusion's status (rebuttable or absolute) is in POL-MTR-002, which is not supplied. Authority limits by level are missing.
findings.explanation: Total incurred is 11,200 across a single payment of 11,200, so there is no payment splitting under 2.2. Dual approval is recorded (L3 and L4, second at L3 or above). The level-based limits and the nature of exclusion POL-MTR-002:3.2 are not in the supplied clauses, so approver authority for this amount and for setting aside the exclusion cannot be confirmed. A reviewer needs the authority limit table and POL-MTR-002 to decide. If the exclusion is absolute, the override itself is a breach.

findings.rule: 3.2 requires the second approver to be independent of the handler and not report directly to the first approver. The claim facts do not record reporting lines or the handler identity, and 3.3 requires approver identities, roles and timestamps, but only levels are recorded.

evidence.value: Insured disputes the breath test result. Team leader (L3) set aside the intoxication exclusion as a goodwill gesture given 12 years' tenure; second approval by Claims Manager (L4).

findings.explanation: The Claims Manager (L4) approving after a team leader (L3) may mean a reporting-line relationship, which 3.2 prohibits. The facts do not confirm the reporting lines or that identities and timestamps were recorded, so independence and recording cannot be verified.

findings.rule: Fraud score 0 falls in the Low band (0-29): normal handling; no mandatory referral triggers (5.1) are evidenced; no enhanced verification, SIU referral or block is required.
findings.explanation: No fraud indicators are recorded, so the sum of triggered points is 0 and the recorded score of 0 is correct. The Low band requires only normal handling. None of the 5.1 triggers is evidenced: the claimed value is far below AUD 250,000, and no indicators, staff involvement or repeat claims are recorded. No SIU referral or settlement block was required, so the absence of both is compliant. The intoxication exclusion override is outside the fraud area and is not assessed here.

findings.rule: Decision-stage and settlement-stage documents required for the claim must be on file before the decision to accept (POL-DOC-005 1.3, Appendix A). Value-based documents apply above AUD 10,000, 50,000 and 100,000.
findings.explanation: Required codes for this accepted motor repair claim of AUD 12,400 with the driver in control: CLAIM_FORM, ID_VERIFIED, DRIVER_LICENCE, PHOTOS, POLICE_EVENT, LICENCE_VERIFIED (claimed amount over 10,000), REPAIR_QUOTE_ACCREDITED, ASSESSMENT_REPORT, VEHICLE_HISTORY_CHECK and BANK_VERIFIED. All are on file, and docs_complete_date (2026-08-14) is before the decision date (2026-08-19). EXCEPTION_EVIDENCE is also on file, as clause 3.7 requires where a rebuttal is relied on. STAT_DEC, PPSR_SEARCH, INDEPENDENT_ASSESSMENT, TP_DETAILS, CTP_REFERENCE, total-loss documents and GST_DECLARATION are not triggered. The presence of EXCEPTION_EVIDENCE does not validate the recorded exclusion override, which is outside this area.

findings.rule: Acknowledge within 2 business days; decide standard claim within 20 business days of docs-complete and within 4 months of lodgement; communicate decision within 5 business days; pay within 10 business days of acceptance; status update at least every 20 business days.
findings.calculation: Ack 1 <= 2; decision 3 <= 20 from docs complete; within 4 months; communication 0 <= 5; payment 3 <= 10; contact gap 4 <= 20.
findings.explanation: All service-level timeframes were met. The decision's other issues, such as the exclusion override, are outside this area.

findings.rule: Excess = basic excess plus any additional excess; net = gross minus excess and ITC deduction. Driver aged 35 with 17 full licence years, so no young/inexperienced additional excess; driver is policyholder (listed NA), so no unlisted excess.
findings.explanation: Excess, ITC (claimant not GST registered, so nil), and net payment are correct. Not a total loss and no recovery applies. The settlement arithmetic is correct. Whether the exclusion override was permissible is outside this area.

fraud: fraud score bands and required actions

documents required for a claim of AUD 12400
